title: Walk the floor
intro: Four steps, one script that grows. The robot stands on a floor 600 pixels wide with a wall at each end. Its place is a Vector2 this time, it walks by direction and time, it cannot leave the floor, and it remembers which way it faces.

steps.title: Place the robot with a Vector2
steps.prompt: The floor runs from x = 0 on the left to x = 600 on the right. Declare a variable at the top of the script (a member variable) called `position` holding `Vector2(300, 0)`, so the robot starts in the middle, and another called `speed` holding the number `150`: pixels per second. A Vector2 holds an x and a y in one value; the robot only ever moves along x here, and y stays 0.
steps.starter:
# The robot's place on the floor, and its walking speed.
# Declare both member variables here.
hints: `Vector2(300, 0)` is a value like any other: it can go on the right of `=` in a `var` line.
`var position = Vector2(300, 0)` and `var speed = 150`, both at the top of the script.

docs.name: Vector2(x, y)
docs.what: makes a value holding an x and a y; position.x reads the x part

docs.name: var
docs.what: declares a variable; at the top of a script it is a member variable that every function can use

steps.title: Move by direction and time
steps.prompt: Write `move`, which takes two parameters: `direction`, a Vector2 such as `Vector2(1, 0)` for right or `Vector2(-1, 0)` for left, and `delta`, the time in seconds. It adds `direction * speed * delta` to `position`. Half a second to the right at speed 150 moves the robot 75 pixels. The buttons beside the stage call move with a direction and half a second.

tests.name: Half a second to the right moves 75
One second to the left moves 150 back

hints: A Vector2 times a number scales both parts: `Vector2(1, 0) * 75` is `Vector2(75, 0)`.
Add the whole product to position in one line: `position += direction * speed * delta`.

docs.what: a Vector2 times a number multiplies its x and its y
adds to a variable in place; works on Vector2 too

steps.title: Walk every frame
steps.prompt: Now the robot keeps walking on its own. Declare a member variable `walking` starting at `Vector2(0, 0)`, meaning standing still. Write `go_left`, which sets walking to `Vector2(-1, 0)`, `go_right`, which sets it to `Vector2(1, 0)`, and `stop`, which sets it back to `Vector2(0, 0)`. Then write `_process(delta)`, which calls `move(walking, delta)` every frame. One second of frames after go_right moves the robot 150 pixels.

tests.name: Standing still, a second of frames changes nothing
go_left then half a second reaches 225

hints: The three small functions only assign a Vector2 to `walking`; nothing else.
`_process` has one job: `move(walking, delta)`. When walking is (0, 0) the product is (0, 0) and nothing moves.
If the robot moves at once without a button press, check that `walking` starts at `Vector2(0, 0)`.

docs.name: _process(delta)
docs.what: a function Godot calls every frame; delta is that frame's length in seconds

docs.name: Vector2(0, 0)
docs.what: the zero vector: no movement in either direction

steps.title: Stay inside the edges, face the way you walk
steps.prompt: Two finishing touches. First the walls: after moving, if `position.x` went below the number `0`, set `position.x` to `0`; if it went above the number `600`, set it to `600`. Put those two checks in `move`, right after the addition. Second, a member variable `facing` starting at `"right"`: `go_left` sets it to `"left"` and `go_right` sets it to `"right"`. The stage shows the facing in its status line.

tests.name: Walking right for three seconds stops at the wall
Walking left for three seconds stops at 0
A direct move past the edge is held at 600
go_right after go_left faces right again

hints: `position.x` can be read and assigned on its own: `position.x = 0` leaves y as it was.
Two separate `if` lines after the addition, one for each wall.
`facing` is text: `"left"` and `"right"` with the quotes, set inside go_left and go_right.

docs.name: position.x
docs.what: the x part of a Vector2; it can be read or assigned by itself

docs.name: if
docs.what: runs the indented lines only when the condition is true

godot: Open Godot and make a new project called Robot Walks.
Create a 2D scene with a Node2D root named Robot, and give it a Sprite2D child using icon.svg as its texture.
Attach a script to Robot. In Godot the node already has a `position` that is a Vector2, so declare only `var speed = 150`, `var walking = Vector2(0, 0)` and `var facing = "right"`.
Copy move, go_left, go_right, stop and _process into the script, and let move change the node's own position.
In `func _ready():` call `go_right()`. Run the scene (F6): the icon walks right and stops at x = 600.
Change the call to `go_left()` and run again: it walks left and stops at the left wall.
Add a Label child and, in go_left and go_right, set `$Label.text = facing` so the word shows over the robot.
Try `speed = 300` and watch it cross the floor in half the time.
